subject: Post-call recap: Audit logs & data access follow-ups (FinCoBank)
messages:
From: Jordan Blake <jordan.blake@redwood.inference>
To: Alice Gomez <alice.gomez@fincobank.com>
Cc: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.inference>, Sean Gallagher <sean.gallagher@redwood.inference>
Date: Mon, 20 Jul 2026 14:05:00 -0700
Subject: Post-call recap: Audit logs & data access follow-ups (FinCoBank)

Hi Alice — thanks again for the call earlier. Quick recap and proposed next steps so we’re aligned: 

Recap:
- You asked for audit log evidence showing who accessed customer data and when (both UI/API and service/system actions).
- Desired export formats: CSV and newline-delimited JSON (NDJSON).
- Retention expectation: 13 months (you mentioned regulatory requirement).
- PII handling: you prefer hashed identifiers in exports; will need confirmation on what fields we can hash.

Our next steps (proposed):
1) We’ll produce a sample export (CSV) showing schema and a small data sample for your review — target within 48 hours.
2) Provide the audit-log schema PDF and a short note on retention and retention controls.
3) Confirm on-demand export mechanics (self-serve vs. support ticket) and how to request a historical export.
4) Provide mapping of internal/service accounts vs. customer-facing actors.

Please confirm the exact columns you need in the export (timestamp, actor_id, actor_type, action, resource, ip, request_id, etc.) and whether UTC timestamps are required. Once you confirm, we’ll include them in the sample.

Thanks — Jordan
Jordan Blake
Account Executive | Redwood Inference
jordan.blake@redwood.inference
Mobile: (415) 555-0123

Attachment: none in this initial note

From: Alice Gomez <alice.gomez@fincobank.com>
To: Jordan Blake <jordan.blake@redwood.inference>
Cc: FinCoBank Compliance <compliance@fincobank.com>
Date: Mon, 20 Jul 2026 15:10:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Post-call recap: Audit logs & data access follow-ups (FinCoBank)

Thanks Jordan — that recap looks right. A few clarifications and must-haves from our compliance team: 

Required columns in exports (minimum):
- timestamp (ISO 8601, UTC)
- actor_id (customer-facing ID where available)
- actor_type (user, service_account, admin)
- action (read, write, delete, export, config_change)
- resource (resource path / object id)
- ip_address
- request_id / trace_id
- result/status (success/failure)

Retention and residency:
- Retention: 13 months for audit logs; we need confirmation that logs beyond 13 months can be pulled on request for e-discovery.
- Residency: logs for our EU data must reside in EU region. Please confirm regional segregation options.

PII handling:
- We prefer hashed PII in exports (one-way salted hashes). Please indicate which fields you will hash and if we can provide the salt or if Redwood will manage salts.

Evidence and attestations:
- Provide a sample export (CSV) and the schema PDF.
- Please include a short statement (1-2 paragraphs) describing how you record service-initiated actions vs. customer-initiated actions (i.e., how you populate actor_type and how service accounts are labeled).

Export mechanics:
- We need to know whether exports are self-serve via the Console/API or if they require a support request. For support requests, include expected SLA for export delivery.

Looking forward to the sample. CCed compliance@fincobank.com for visibility.

Best,
Alice Gomez
Security & Compliance Lead | FinCoBank
alice.gomez@fincobank.com

Hi Jordan / Alice — thanks, looping in the artifacts requested. Summary below and attached files.

What we attached:
- redwood_audit_log_sample.csv (CSV sample, 12 rows) — columns: timestamp_utc, actor_id_hashed, actor_type, action, resource, ip_address, request_id, status
- redwood_audit_log_schema.pdf — schema description and field definitions, includes guidance on which fields we can/should hash
- soc2-summary.pdf — short SOC 2 coverage summary and link to full report request process

Notes / answers to Alice’s questions:
- Timestamps: all exports use ISO 8601 in UTC by default.
- Retention: default retention is 13 months. We can retain in-region (EU) if the account is configured for EU residency — Sean, please confirm configuration steps (see cc). Historical exports beyond retention are possible on request and handled via support ticket with a 5-business-day SLA for exports older than retention window.
- PII hashing: we provide one-way salted hashes for identifiers in exports. Redwood manages salts (not shared). If FinCo requires salt management, we can discuss a custom arrangement under an enterprise contract.
- Actor labeling: we surface actor_type as 'user', 'service_account', or 'admin'. Service accounts are prefixed with 'svc-' in the actor_id field and mapped in the schema PDF. The attached schema includes a mapping table for internal service accounts vs. customer-facing actors.
- Export mechanics: exports can be triggered via the Console (Project > Exports > New export) or via API (POST /v1/logs/exports). Small example (curl) is in the schema PDF. For one-off historical exports beyond retention, please open a SupportTicket (SupportTicket#RB-45812); SLA is 5 business days.

We’ve attached the sample files referenced above. If you want, we can also provide NDJSON export; let me know preference.

Thanks — Marissa
Marissa Cole
Security Solutions | Redwood Inference
marissa.cole@redwood.inference
